subject: Marketplace contract Q&A: cloud residency & deletion across AWS/GCP/Azure

Subject: Residency & retention mapping for marketplace listing

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the quick onboarding call yesterday. As we move toward the Marketplace listing, procurement pushed a short checklist around data residency and deletion guarantees that we need to surface in the listing and the technical FAQ. A couple of specific asks from our legal team: 

- For customers that buy via our AWS/GCP/Azure marketplace listings, can Redwood guarantee that customer data (inference requests and derived embeddings) is stored only in the customer-selected cloud region?
- How does Redwood handle retention and automated deletion requests? Does deletion propagate to backups and snapshots?
- For multi-cloud marketplace agreements, do you provide a single DPA clause or per-cloud appendices?

I've attached the marketplace vendor template and the checklist. Can your security or solutions team provide short, snappy Q&A items we can paste into our listing?

Appreciate it —
Lisa
Marketplaces & Partnerships
CloudMarketplace Inc.

Hi Lisa / team —

Below are concise Q&A items you can paste into the marketplace listing or the vendor FAQ. Kept them short for marketplace UX, with a follow-on note pointing to technical artifacts (we can add the residency matrix link).

1) "Where is my data stored?"
Redwood stores customer data (requests, generated outputs, and embeddings) only in the cloud region selected at provisioning. For Dedicated and Private deployments, compute and storage are provisioned in the customer's chosen region; for Hosted API marketplace SKUs we route and pin customers to their requested region when available. See residency matrix for region availability per cloud.

2) "Can you delete my data on request?"
Yes. Redwood processes customer deletion requests via the Console or API. Deletion removes live objects, model caches, and associated metadata. We also provide a deletion request workflow for customers to trigger and verify erasure; for contractual commitments we can add a deletion SLA to the DPA.

3) "Do deletions include backups and snapshots?"
We commit to removing data from primary storage and our application tier within the deletion SLA. For backups and snapshots, we operate on a predictable retention schedule; we will either (a) purge customer-specific snapshots within the agreed SLA window or (b) provide an explicit exception/certification that data contained in immutable backups will be marked for deletion and removed at the next snapshot lifecycle window. For Marketplace/partner deals we recommend the latter approach with a stated maximum window (e.g., 30–60 days) to align with provider-level snapshot retention.

Additional technical notes:
- We support KMS-integrated encryption with customer-managed keys (CMK) in AWS/Azure/GCP to ensure keys never leave the selected region when requested.
- Audit logs and access logs are available for export and can be scoped to region; we retain logs per the customer's retention setting and can provide exportable evidence on deletion actions.

I'll attach the residency matrix and a deletion flow diagram. Rafael — can you add a short operations note about cross-cloud fallbacks (if a region is temporarily unavailable we default to policy-based routing; we do not fail open to other regions without customer approval).

—Vivek
Director of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency & retention mapping for marketplace listing

Hi Lisa —

Quick operational points to drop into the marketplace FAQ and the vendor listing. I kept the language customer-facing and non-technical.

- Region assignment: When provisioning, customers choose their cloud provider and region. Redwood deploys compute and stores artifacts (inputs, outputs, KV cache, embeddings) in that region by default. If a customer needs data residency guarantees in a specific availability zone, we need that captured in the order form.

- Deletion process: Customers can request deletion from the Console or via our API; deletion triggers a workflow that invalidates KV caches, removes live data, and issues a snapshot purge request. We will confirm completion with an exported activity log within the deletion SLA.

- Backups: Practical note — some managed snapshot systems (particularly provider-managed backups) may have provider-imposed retention. For marketplace agreements we recommend calling out a maximum snapshot purge window (we've used 30 days for similar Marketplace partners).

- DPA structure: We propose a single base DPA with cloud-specific appendices that list region availability and CMK guidance per cloud. That keeps legal review lean while being explicit about provider constraints.

If the partner wants specific wording for the marketplace listing, I can produce a 1-paragraph blurb per bullet.

Thanks,
Rafael
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — this is exactly what we needed. A few follow-ups from our procurement/legal side: 

- Can you commit to a maximum snapshot purge window of 30 days for marketplace customers (we'll put this in the marketplace appendix)?
- For customers who require the encryption key to be customer-managed, can we add a short line confirming CMK support per cloud?
- Kenji from our AWS marketplace team asked whether Redwood can provide a short statement confirming that the region selected in the AWS marketplace order will be honored by Redwood for both compute and storage. He noted that sometimes third-party vendors create a single global tenant, which is a non-starter for some enterprise buyers.

If you can reply with one-line confirmations for each, we'll draft the appendix and share an initial marketplace entry by end of week.

Best,
Lisa
